messages.content: What is the earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?

function.name: get_earliest_reference
function.description: Retrieve the earliest historical reference of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source.description: Source to fetch the reference. Default is 'scriptures'

message.content:
**Earliest non‑Christian historical reference to Jesus Christ**

| Source | Date (approx.) | Passage | Significance |
|--------|----------------|---------|--------------|
| **Josephus – *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 18, Chapter 3** | 93–94 CE (written by Josephus in the 90s CE) | “Now there was a wise man, and it was said that he was a doer of wonderful works… He was called **Christ**. … He was crucified by Pontius Pilate at the time of the procurator Tiberius.” | This is the first surviving mention of Jesus in a contemporary, non‑Christian source. It appears in a Jewish historian’s account of the period, and it is widely accepted by scholars as authentic (though the passage has a later Christian interpolation). |

### Why Josephus is considered the earliest

1. **Contemporaneity** – Josephus was a first‑century Jewish historian who lived during the reign of Emperor Vespasian (AD 69–79) and wrote his *Antiquities* in the 90s CE.  
2. **Independent of Christian tradition** – The text was written before the New Testament books were compiled, so it is not derived from Christian writings.  
3. **Historical context** – Josephus refers to Pontius Pilate, the Roman prefect who executed Jesus, and places the event in the reign of Tiberius, matching the biblical chronology.

### The passage (Testimonium Flavianum)

> “Now there was a wise man, and it was said that he was a doer of wonderful works… He was called **Christ**. … He was crucified by Pontius Pilate at the time of the procurator Tiberius.”  
> — *Antiquities* 18.3.3 (excerpt)

Scholars note that the passage contains a few phrases that are almost certainly later Christian additions (e.g., “He was the Christ”), but the core elements—his existence, his title “Christ,” and his crucifixion under Pilate—are considered historically reliable.

### Other early references (later than Josephus)

| Source | Date | Key mention |
|--------|------|-------------|
| **Tacitus – *Annals* 15.44** | 116 CE | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate.” |
| **Pliny the Younger – *Letters* 1.10** | 112 CE | Describes early Christians worshipping Christ as a god. |
| **Babylonian Talmud** | 3rd–5th CE (compiled later) | Mentions “Yeshu” (Jesus) in a brief passage. |

These are important corroborations but come after Josephus’s account.

---

**Bottom line:** The earliest surviving historical record that mentions Jesus Christ outside of Christian scripture is Josephus’s *Antiquities of the Jews* (c. 93–94 CE). It provides an independent, contemporary acknowledgment of Jesus’s existence, title, and crucifixion.
